subject.title: [Feature]: Add gateway-side circuit breaker for unhealthy sessions after consecutive failures

question: What session-health breaker contract should OpenClaw core own before implementation: a unified receipt/state model, a narrow no-progress counter, or deferral to existing narrower guard tracks?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing failure taxonomy, persistence, defaults, cooldown or half-open behavior, auto-rotation, and UI/operator recovery semantics is a product/config contract decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Design unified session-health receipts
options.body: Define failure signature, counters, last success, retry admission, suggested recovery, persistence, and operator controls before adding runtime enforcement.

options.title: Land a narrow no-progress breaker
options.body: Limit the first change to a bounded consecutive no-progress counter in the embedded run loop and leave receipts, persistence, cooldowns, and auto-rotation as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Defer to narrower guards
options.body: Keep idle-timeout, tool-loop, post-compaction, provider, cron, and subagent guard tracks separate and narrow this umbrella request later.

recommendation.title: Design unified session-health receipts
recommendation.body: Define failure signature, counters, last success, retry admission, suggested recovery, persistence, and operator controls before adding runtime enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest current and adjacent history across the embedded run-loop retry, idle-timeout, and post-compaction guard surfaces.
